what_changed: Adds a debug-capture mode to `dispatch_subagent` in `scripts/orchestrator_runner.py`, gated by the `DOCS_AGENT_DEBUG_DIR` environment variable. When the gate is on, dispatch switches to Claude's stream-JSON output format and records the source-collector agent's complete tool-call sequence (raw NDJSON + a structured tool-use summary) to disk; when the gate is off, dispatch behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. Two pure helper functions (`_extract_final_assistant_text` and `_summarize_tool_use`) back the new path, each covered by new TDD tests (10 new tests, 174 total passing). The PR also ships a 5-run Mode B baseline measurement doc that categorizes each run as A (zero tool calls), B (tools called then discarded), C (legitimately empty), or D (errored). Four of five runs fell into Category A — the source-collector emitted canonical empty JSON in a single ~3–6 s turn without ever invoking a tool.
why: CCE-10 hypothesized that the source-collector's failure to surface real PR data was a prompt or policy gap rather than broken tool plumbing. This PR instruments the dispatch path to capture ground-truth tool-call traces and runs a 5-run baseline to test that hypothesis. The results confirm it: the agent never calls `gh pr list`; it returns an empty-result JSON immediately without any tool invocation. The data unblocks CCE-13, which will harden the source-collector system prompt with a mandatory tool-call step before producing output.
notes: The 25 raw measurement artifacts (5 runs × 5 file types: .meta.json, .prompt.txt, .stderr.txt, .stdout.txt, .stream.jsonl) are data files, not narrative docs; no separate doc targets are needed for them. CCE-13 (system-prompt hardening) will require a new summarizer pass once its PR merges.
